turns.query: Compare FY2024 SBA 7(a) lending geography with the same insured bank's 2025-06-30 Summary of Deposits geography across the 50 states and District of Columbia. Preserve every reported SBA row, use the canonical unpadded FDIC certificate to match lenders, and use SOD's state-abbreviation-to-state-FIPS correspondence for the 51-jurisdiction QCEW bridge. Retain lenders present in both sources with at least 500 FY2024 SBA rows. Within each lender form approval-dollar and branch-deposit-dollar state distributions, calculate total-variation distance as one half of the sum of absolute share differences, and rank descending with lender name and FDIC certificate ascending as tie-breakers. Define distribution overlap as the jurisdiction-wise sum of the smaller approval and deposit shares, equivalently one minus TVD. Report the eligible-lender count; leader name and certificate; its SBA row count, gross approvals, deposits, positive-approval and positive-deposit jurisdiction counts, TVD, distribution overlap, and TVD margin over the runner-up. Explain what the mismatch measure represents.

For that selected lender, identify its largest-approval jurisdiction and report its approvals, approval share, deposits and deposit share. Separately identify its largest-deposit jurisdiction and report its deposits, deposit share, approvals and approval share. Break any state-level tie by USPS abbreviation ascending. Explain which side of the two distributions drives the turn-1 distance result.

Overlay the preliminary retrospective 2025 QCEW private-employment vintage. For every one of the 51 jurisdictions, calculate 2024-to-2025 growth from annual-average employment levels and define the negative-growth set from the unrounded level calculation. Report the matched-jurisdiction count and negative-growth count. For the selected lender, report within that set the SBA row count, gross approvals, share of all its FY2024 approvals, gross approvals minus SBA-guaranteed approvals, SOD deposits and share of all its deposits. Also report the negative-growth jurisdiction with its largest approval dollars and that jurisdiction's calculated employment growth, breaking an approval tie by USPS abbreviation. Explain the grain and vintage limits of this macro overlay.

Match the selected FDIC certificate to the 2024-12-31 Call Report and report the match count, RSSD ID, legal name and domestic-office total equity. Then run a sensitivity: assume a loss equal to 10% of the prior turn's gross-minus-guaranteed FY2024 approvals in negative-employment jurisdictions, hold everything else fixed, and report the loss, pro forma domestic-office equity, and loss as a percentage of reported equity. Explain what this calculation does and does not establish about the bank's credit loss and capital position.
